Military Channel 52-wk Retail Sales Run Rate
Record FY2018: revenue +45% to $52.6M, North America +62%; growth volume-led, no pricing tailwind.
Central strategic move: China model restructured to royalty-licensing with Qifeng - eliminates further direct China investment, refocuses working capital on North America.
Q4 net loss to common improved dramatically to $0.893M from $5.3M as ~$5M of China marketing spend rolled off.
Gross margin compressed FY (40% vs 42.7%) on new-account promotional allowances/slotting, lower Asia margins, elevated freight/production costs.
Marquee retail wins: Target (~1,200 stores), CVS (nationwide authorized), DICK'S (250+); added Food Lion, Hannaford, Circle K.
DSD network build-out with Anheuser-Busch, Keurig Dr. Pepper, PepsiCo, MillerCoors network partners - key fix for Target out-of-stocks and convenience execution.
Europe down 17% FY on promotional/flavor-launch timing and distributor inventory reduction; Peach Vibe launch driving share gains, Nordic to normalize in 2019.
Energy category 'renaissance' - migration to healthier functional energy alternatives, like sparkling water disrupted CSDs.
Inventory roughly doubled at year-end as deliberate working-capital pull-forward ahead of summer beverage season.
Rockstar Energy lawsuit disclosed; management characterized it as meritless.
No 2019 guidance provided; management cited 'plan A/B/C' liquidity levers and asserted no expected dilution despite prior-year capital raise.
Competitive moat: trade-secret formula (not patented), six clinical studies, prior NAD/litigation wins; views Bang/VPX as complementary (different demographics).
Management tone confident and forward-leaning, emphasizing pivot to profitable North America growth.
Sell-through trends, door-count plans and SKU additions at Target, CVS and convenience channel.

Target expanded from ~500-store test to ~1,200 stores (3 SKUs, 4th hopeful), sell-through above expectations though warehouse fulfillment caused out-of-stocks. CVS reached 1,000+ stores (3 SKUs), authorized nationwide for 2019, fulfilling via CVS DCs.
Update on adding domestic co-packers and advantages of new distribution partners for 2019.

Convenience opportunity (only ~10% ACV) leveraged via new DSD partners (AB, Keurig Dr. Pepper, independent Pepsi bottlers) for incremental distribution and in-stock execution. 4 co-packers active, 3 onboarding - ready for summer season.
Is the Nordic region normalized or normalizing, given Q4 looked stronger?
Nordic turning to normalized levels; FY -17% decline concentrated in Q1-Q2 2018. Peach Vibe flavor launch driving market-share gains; more flavor innovation planned for 2019.
Lavit deal - locations, distribution, geographic reach and impact on COGS/packaging expenses.
Lavit brings Celsius into new at-work channel via powder cups; launched with Orange powder, working on 2019 innovation. Lavit aggressively placing machines with corporations - incremental revenue.
Anticipated or new marketing partnerships for the coming year.
New partnerships coming; Matt Kahn built aggressive 2019 plan including renewed Tough Mudder partnership, trade activation with key retailers, expanded influencer and digital/social programs.
Current margins, impact of additional co-packers, and whether Q4 one-time margin hits reverse in 2019.
Evaluating co-packer expansion cost trade-off vs guaranteeing summer inventory. Q4 had minor excess-and-obsolescence inventory charges; watching freight to maximize 2019 margins.
Confirming no forward-looking guidance on any metrics for 2019?
Confirmed - no 2019 guidance provided at this time.
China reconciliation, deal close, margin, inventory, competition
Whether China 'negative $1M' reflected Qifeng repaying $950K; whether deal closed; gross margin trajectory; why inventory doubled; positioning vs Bang/VPX (~$500M revenue).

China item was accrued-expense reconciliation, no cash flow. Definitive agreement executed Jan 1, 2019; capital loan ($10M+, 5-yr) finalized by month-end. ~40% FY2018 margin a reasonable 2019 range, freight/co-packer efficiencies as tailwinds. Higher inventory = summer readiness. Bang/VPX complementary (Bang 18-24, Celsius 24-36, more female-skewed).
Synergies/benefits of being part of the AB and Keurig Dr. Pepper distributor networks.

DSD critical - reliance on wholesale/direct-to-retail caused out-of-stocks. DSD partners visit stores weekly ensuring in-stock position, merchandising/POS, and incremental distribution into local independents - gaining people power plus distribution.
How Food Lion/Hannaford performed; whether strong CVS relationship precludes Walgreens; what prevents larger competitors copying Celsius given no patent.

Food Lion meeting expectations with room to scale; Hannaford performing well (~30-36% organic growth). CVS does not preclude Walgreens. Moat = trade secret (not patent), six clinical studies, NAD review, 2010 class-action win, brand momentum; cited Coca-Cola/Nestle's failed Enviga.
Cash burn, dilution risk, short interest
Challenged no-additional-cash assurance (said same in 2018 then raised capital); will 2019 avoid dilution; any theory on high short interest.

Current plan reflects sufficient operating cash flow with plan A/B/C levers. Ex-Asia, 2017 generated ~$2.6-2.7M and 2018 ~$2.2M positive adjusted EBITDA. On short interest, no control/insight, speculated index-fund activity around Russell 2000/3000 inclusion.
